question:
(i) Using de Broglie’s explanation, obtain Bohr’s angular momentum quantisation condition for an electron in a stable orbit.
(ii) Explain why this quantisation condition describes allowed electron orbits and not the size of the nucleus.

options.A:
(i) The electron orbit is stable when $2\pi r=\lambda/ n$, giving $mvr=\dfrac{h}{2\pi n}$.
(ii) This relation determines the radius of the nucleus.
options.B:
(i) For a stable orbit, the electron matter wave forms a standing wave: $2\pi r=n\lambda$. With $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{mv}$, this gives $mvr=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$.
(ii) This quantisation describes allowed electron orbits around the nucleus. It does not determine nuclear size, which is a property of the compact nucleus.
options.C:
(i) de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda=\dfrac{mv}{h}$, giving $mvr=2\pi nh$.
(ii) The condition measures the number of neutrons in the nucleus.
options.D:
(i) All circular electron orbits are allowed because electron waves never interfere.
(ii) Nuclear radius is obtained from the electron's standing-wave condition.
